children: Hewlett Packard Enterprise, a hybrid-cloud infrastructure vendor

, unveiled plans to support Nvidia OpenShell and introduce Vera CPU rack infrastructure, while shares traded at $54.60, down 6.14% at 11.20am EST on Thursday. The push targets businesses that need tighter control over autonomous AI systems, sensitive data and computing resources. More AI hardware gets HPE through the door. Security and governance could help it capture more spending once inside.

The earnings test is already taking shape. HPE's fiscal-third-quarter results showed Cloud and AI revenue of $9.0 billion, up 25.4% from a year earlier, while the segment's operating margin reached 17%, versus 7%. That 10-percentage-point improvement matters: growth delivered a much stronger profit contribution. The question now is whether new AI deployments can sustain that profitability as customers demand more complex systems and support.

The valuation leaves little room for sloppy execution. The chart places the shares 90.98% above the $28.59 GF Value estimate, suggesting substantial growth expectations remain priced in despite the selloff. That estimate is a valuation reference, not a guaranteed destination. HPE's next hurdle is turning its broader AI offering into revenue and cash flow while defending the margin gains it has already delivered.

title: HPE Stocks Fall 6.14% as Secure Agentic Stack Broadens
